topico: glicogenio (treino de estilo AnKing — SANDBOX, nao vai pro deck vivo)

cards.Text: Glycogen is a branched storage polymer of {{c1::glucose}}
cards.Extra: Highly branched for rapid mobilization. img

cards.Text: The linear glucose linkages in glycogen are {{c1::α-1,4}} glycosidic bonds
The branch-point linkages in glycogen are {{c1::α-1,6}} glycosidic bonds
Glycogen is stored mainly in {{c1::liver}} and {{c2::skeletal muscle}}
cards.Extra: Liver ~10% by weight, muscle ~1-2% but larger total mass. img

cards.Text: Glycogen synthesis is nucleated by the primer protein {{c1::glycogenin}}
The activated glucose donor for glycogen synthesis is {{c1::UDP-glucose}}
Glucose-6-phosphate is converted to glucose-1-phosphate by {{c1::phosphoglucomutase}}
UDP-glucose is formed from glucose-1-phosphate by {{c1::UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase}}
The rate-limiting enzyme of glycogenesis is {{c1::glycogen synthase}}
cards.Extra: Adds glucose via α-1,4 bonds. img

cards.Text: Branches in glycogen are created by {{c1::branching enzyme}}
cards.Extra: Transfers a ~7-residue block to an α-1,6 position. img

cards.Text: The rate-limiting enzyme of glycogenolysis is {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}}
Glycogen phosphorylase cleaves α-1,4 bonds by {{c1::phosphorolysis}}, releasing glucose-1-phosphate
Glycogen phosphorylase requires the cofactor {{c1::pyridoxal phosphate}} (vitamin B6)
Glycogen phosphorylase stops {{c1::4}} residues from a branch point, leaving a limit dextrin
The {{c1::debranching enzyme}} removes the α-1,6 branch, releasing free glucose
About {{c1::8}}% of glycogen is released as free glucose (from branch points); the rest is glucose-1-phosphate
Glycogen synthase is active when {{c1::dephosphorylated}}
Glycogen phosphorylase is active when {{c1::phosphorylated}}
Glucagon and epinephrine raise {{c1::cAMP}} via adenylyl cyclase
cAMP activates {{c1::protein kinase A}} (PKA)
PKA phosphorylates and activates {{c1::phosphorylase kinase}}
Phosphorylase kinase phosphorylates and activates {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}}
PKA also phosphorylates and {{c1::inactivates}} glycogen synthase
cards.Extra: One signal: breakdown on, synthesis off. img

cards.Text: Insulin activates {{c1::protein phosphatase 1}} (PP1)
cards.Extra: Dephosphorylates the cascade: synthesis on, breakdown off. img

cards.Text: In liver, glucose binds phosphorylase a and exposes it to {{c1::PP1}}
cards.Extra: Links high glucose to storage. img

cards.Text: Glycogen synthase is allosterically activated by {{c1::glucose-6-phosphate}}
In muscle, glycogen phosphorylase b is allosterically activated by {{c1::AMP}}
In muscle, glycogen phosphorylase is activated by {{c1::Ca2+}}/calmodulin during contraction
cards.Extra: Calmodulin is a subunit of phosphorylase kinase. img

cards.Text: Muscle epinephrine acts on glycogen via {{c1::β-adrenergic}} receptors
Liver glycogen serves to maintain {{c1::blood glucose}}
Muscle glycogen fuels {{c1::the muscle itself}} (cannot export glucose)
Muscle cannot release free glucose because it lacks {{c1::glucose-6-phosphatase}}
Free glucose is released from G6P by {{c1::glucose-6-phosphatase}} in the ER
Von Gierke disease (type I) is deficiency of {{c1::glucose-6-phosphatase}}
Von Gierke presents with severe fasting {{c1::hypoglycemia}} and hepatomegaly
cards.Extra: Also lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, hyperlipidemia. img

cards.Text: Pompe disease (type II) is deficiency of lysosomal {{c1::acid α-glucosidase}} (acid maltase)
Pompe classically causes {{c1::cardiomegaly}} and hypotonia
Cori disease (type III) is deficiency of {{c1::debranching enzyme}}
Cori disease accumulates {{c1::limit dextrin}} (short outer branches)
cards.Extra: Milder than von Gierke; normal lactate. img

cards.Text: McArdle disease (type V) is deficiency of muscle {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}} (myophosphorylase)
McArdle presents with exercise intolerance and {{c1::no rise in lactate}} on exertion
Andersen disease (type IV) is deficiency of {{c1::branching enzyme}}
Hers disease (type VI) is deficiency of liver {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}}
In the fed state, glycogen synthesis is driven by {{c1::insulin}}
In the fasting state, liver glycogenolysis is driven by {{c1::glucagon}}
Liver glycogen is largely depleted after about {{c1::12-24}} hours of fasting
The bond broken by glycogen phosphorylase is {{c1::α-1,4}}, not α-1,6
cards.Extra: α-1,6 is handled by the debranching enzyme. img

cards.Text: Glucose-1-phosphate from glycogenolysis enters glycolysis after conversion to {{c1::glucose-6-phosphate}}
Phosphorylase kinase has a subunit that is the Ca2+ sensor {{c1::calmodulin}}
The two enzymatic activities of the debranching enzyme are 4-α-glucanotransferase and {{c1::α-1,6-glucosidase}}
